name: ZH Man Sichuan (comic boast)
sounds_like: Mandarin with a Sichuan accent, performed as a comic character voice: median 245 Hz, far above this library other male speakers, swinging across 18.3 semitones up past 398 Hz. Mid-bright (centroid 1722 Hz), 4.5 onsets per second, 22% silence with pauses to 0.87s for comic beats. The source line is a boast - the speaker calls himself a revered immortal, admits to some baby fat, then insists it cannot hide his striking good looks.
casts_well_as: Comic Chinese-language character, boastful buffoon, cartoon immortal or deity, broad regional comedy.
avoid_for: English dialogue - the reference is Sichuanese-accented Mandarin and both language and accent transfer. Also unusable for any serious or threatening register.
note: Read the 245 Hz median with care: Mandarin is a tone language, so measured pitch range is inflated by lexical tone that carries meaning rather than emotion. The high register here is a deliberate comic falsetto, not the speaker natural voice.
